clue.text: Queen of Saskatchewan

parts.note: the Latin word for a queen is also the name of the provincial capital of Saskatchewan, so the city is that province's queen

explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the Canadian province of Saskatchewan bears the Latin word for a queen.

clue.text: It's simply a matter of principle

definitions.text: It's simply a matter of principle

parts.words: It's simply a matter of principle
parts.note: principle read as a basic first element, something simple to learn rather than a moral stance

explanation.definitionFit: A basic element or first principle of a subject, learned at the very start.

clue.text: Rum and butter material

parts.note: grog is rum diluted with water, the old naval ration
a ram butts with its head, so is a butter

explanation.surface: A recipe calls for rum and butter, as for a hot toddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse fabric of silk mixed with mohair or wool, a historical cloth.

clue.text: The age at which one was " stony "' ?

definitions.text: The age at which one was " stony "' ?

parts.words: The age at which one was " stony "'
parts.note: stony broke read as the prehistoric period when tools were made of stone

explanation.definitionFit: The later prehistoric period when polished stone tools were used, the new stone age.

clue.text: Flying Officer ?

parts.note: read not as an RAF rank but as a bird that shares its name with a military staff officer

explanation.definitionFit: An army staff officer who assists a commander, and also a large Indian stork, so a bird that flies.

clue.text: Not the kind to be heard on a harmonium ?

definitions.text: Not the kind to be heard on a harmonium ?

parts.words: Not the kind to be heard on a harmonium
parts.note: the instrument's name suggests harmony, so a jarring sound would not belong

explanation.definitionFit: A jarring sound clashes with harmony, which the reed organ's name echoes.

clue.text: One of those business relationships

parts.note: a family title used in old slang for the pawnbroker, a business contact

explanation.walkthrough: In old British slang the pawnbroker is called 'uncle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pawnbroker was nicknamed after a parent's brother, so the shop counter becomes a family relation.

clue.text: He might be a great authority on port

definitions.text: He might be a great authority on port

parts.words: He might be a great authority on port
parts.note: port as the left side of a ship, not the wine, and a senior naval commander

explanation.definitionFit: A top-ranking naval officer commands ships, whose left side is called port.

clue.text: " A rosebud set with little wilful" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: " A rosebud set with little wilful" (Tennyson)

parts.words: " A rosebud set with little wilful" (Tennyson)
parts.note: a line from Tennyson's Maud with its last word left blank to be filled

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank clue: the printed page shows a dash where the line's final word goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp prickles on a rose stem complete Tennyson's line describing Maud.

clue.text: It's extra, of course, in magical style

parts.note: super as a prefix means extra or beyond
naturally means of course, as in a reply

explanation.surface: A conjuror shrugs that the bonus trick was obviously done with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond the laws of nature, so by means of magic or the occult.

clue.text: Examples of " double-talk " ?

parts.note: double-talk taken literally: talk between two people, dramatic pieces for a pair of speakers

explanation.definitionFit: Dialogues written for exactly two performers are talk for a pair, double in the literal sense.

clue.text: Relief work that came to nothing

parts.note: taken as written
O, the round zero figure, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An artist's sculpted panel project fizzled out.
explanation.definitionFit: A carving in raised relief, such as a profile cut in shell or stone, is a classic example of relief work.

clue.text: It is reversed in code as a joint affair

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the code's name, as the clue says it is in code

parts.note: Morse is the dot-and-dash telegraph code

indicators.note: the clue says the little word is turned around, so it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cryptographer notes a message is written backwards, a shared enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns IT into TI, and 'in' puts it inside MORSE to give MOR-TI-SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot cut in timber to take a tenon is a woodworking joint, hence a joint affair.

clue.text: Finished the chicken-pen, so they won't do this to the garden

definitions.text: so they won't do this to the garden

parts.note: over means finished, as in the game is over
a run is an enclosure for keeping hens

explanation.surface: Once the hen enclosure is built, the birds will no longer swarm across the flowerbeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last part: with a run made, the chickens won't spread over and swamp the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To swarm across and swamp a place, as loose hens might a flowerbed, is a verb sense meaning to invade in numbers.

clue.text: " Sweet Echo, sweetest, that liv'st unseen Within thy airy shell " (Milton)

definitions.text: " Sweet Echo, sweetest, that liv'st unseen Within thy airy shell " (Milton)

parts.words: " Sweet Echo, sweetest, that liv'st unseen Within thy airy shell " (Milton)
parts.note: a quotation from Milton's masque Comus with one word gap after 'sweetest' to be filled

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank clue: the printed page shows a dash after 'sweetest' where the missing word goes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Echo was a mountain spirit, a minor female deity, so Milton addresses her by that title in Comus.

clue.text: Bank robber who beat about the bush ?

definitions.text: Bank robber who beat about the bush ?

parts.words: Bank robber who beat about the bush
parts.note: the idiom for evading the point is read literally: an outlaw who roamed the Australian outback

explanation.walkthrough: In Australia 'the bush' is the outback, where bushrangers hid between raids.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous nineteenth-century Australian bushranger who held up banks and roamed the outback in homemade armour.

clue.text: One who, luxury notwithstanding, may have a nice pure disposition

indicators.note: the letters are given a new arrangement, disposition meaning placing in order

explanation.surface: Someone who lives in luxury may still have an innocent character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals rearranging A NICE PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotee of fine food and pleasure is given to luxury.

clue.text: One thing one would shrink from being ?

definitions.text: One thing one would shrink from being ?

parts.words: One thing one would shrink from being
parts.note: shrink from read as to become smaller, not to recoil from

explanation.definitionFit: Made smaller or reduced, which is what shrinking does to a thing.

clue.text: Keep over two thousand pounds in town

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written over another comes before it

parts.note: to keep goods is to stock them
a short ton, the US unit, is two thousand pounds in weight

explanation.surface: A banker advises holding large sums in the town branch.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCKTON-on-Tees is a town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockton-on-Tees is an industrial borough in County Durham, a town in north-east England.

clue.text: One has it at one's finger-tips

definitions.text: One has it at one's finger-tips

parts.words: One has it at one's finger-tips
parts.note: the idiom for ready knowledge read literally as a cap worn on a fingertip

explanation.definitionFit: A small metal sewing cap protects the end of a finger while pushing a needle.

clue.text: What's the best thing to entrap her ? Wire netting

indicators.note: the girl is caught within the letters of the closing words, as a net would trap her

explanation.surface: Someone asks how best to catch a lady and suggests chicken wire.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to the question is its own wordplay: the name sits inside 'wIRE NEtting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a stand-in for any particular she.

clue.text: A bit of show-business in court

definitions.text: A bit of show-business in court

parts.words: A bit of show-business in court
parts.note: show taken as displaying evidence, an item produced at a trial

explanation.definitionFit: An object or document shown to a court as evidence, or a showpiece in a gallery.

clue.text: In this, gold may be the centre of attraction

definitions.text: In this, gold may be the centre of attraction

parts.words: In this, gold may be the centre of attraction
parts.note: in archery the bullseye of the board is the gold, the centre everyone aims at

explanation.definitionFit: An archery board, whose bullseye is called the gold, is what shooters aim at.

clue.text: Not necessarily a flighty character

parts.note: flighty taken literally as one who takes flights, not one who is fickle

explanation.definitionFit: A pilot of aircraft takes to the air without being frivolous or capricious.

clue.text: Hearing about this is most depressing

definitions.text: Hearing about this is most depressing

parts.words: Hearing about this is most depressing
parts.note: news of a downward tendency in the figures is gloomy to hear

explanation.definitionFit: A general direction or tendency, as in a downward one in prices or the weather.

clue.text: Cross opponents

parts.note: not angry rivals but the rings that play against X marks in a children's game

explanation.definitionFit: In the pencil game tic-tac-toe one player draws rings and the other draws crosses.

clue.text: One of seven in a novel house

definitions.text: One of seven in a novel house

parts.words: One of seven in a novel house
parts.note: points to Hawthorne's novel about a house with seven pointed roof ends

explanation.definitionFit: The triangular end walls under a pitched roof: Hawthorne's novel names a house with seven of them.

clue.text: For untidy little beasts ?

parts.note: litter read as a brood of young animals and as rubbish, so a receptacle for the mess

explanation.definitionFit: A street receptacle for rubbish, where litter also means a brood of puppies or kittens.

clue.text: This child should be graceful

parts.note: recalls the nursery rhyme that gives each weekday's child a trait, one being full of grace

explanation.walkthrough: The old English rhyme assigns a quality to a child according to the weekday of its birth.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme 'Monday's child is fair of face', the child born on the second weekday is full of grace.

clue.text: Team of joiners ?

parts.note: joiners read as things that join together, and a football club name taken by many sides

explanation.definitionFit: Joined together describes things fastened, and it is the usual name of football clubs such as Manchester's.
